# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="press", slot=N) — N is a key by its place, 1 to 4
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Blind one — the hands. My fingers give me the skeleton of the bomb: a display (printed, unreadable to me), an indicator light (its state is invisible to me), a keypad of four keys which I know only by position, and three wires at positions 1–3 whose colours I can't perceive. My touch also tells me the keypad expects a one-digit entry and nothing has been entered yet.

The communications map, as I work it out: my speech reaches only Mute; my gestures reach Deaf and Mute. Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so the only route for manual knowledge to reach me is Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. Deaf receives only gestures but can talk. So this turn I should hand Mute a complete tactile report plus a proposal for a shared number code, and flash that code openly so both of them have seen the exact signs. I will touch nothing — pressing or cutting before the manual's rules arrive could detonate the bomb, and there is no second attempt.

```
gesture(symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋", "👊"])
speak(to="mute", text="I am the blind one, the hands. I can feel the bomb and act on it, I speak only to you, and I never see gestures. Just now I waved at the deaf one and flashed seven signs; the six after the wave mean, in order: one, two, three, four, five, zero. Please adopt that number code and teach it to the deaf one with gestures. Here is everything my fingers find. There is a display module, but its content is printed and unknown to me. There is an indicator light; its colour and state are unknown to me. There is a keypad of four keys, known to me only by position, one through four; my touch says it expects a one-digit entry and nothing has been entered yet. There are three wires at positions one to three; I feel positions only, no colours. Please look up in the manual: what the display is and means, what the light means, the rule for the keypad code, and how the three wires are to be cut. You cannot speak and I cannot see signs, so please pass your answers to the deaf one by gesture and have them speak the answers aloud to me. I will touch nothing until I hear back.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I am Deaf: I see the bomb and I never hear anything, so your voice never reaches me — only your gestures do. I saw your seven signs but we had no code yet, so I could not read them; if that was a question, resend with the code below. I will describe signs in words, because you will never see mine. Your signs to me: thumbs-up means done; thumbs-down means problem, stop and touch nothing more; raised open palm means waiting; a fist means I am touching or pressing it. If you need Mute to hear a report, just speak aloud to the room — Mute hears you fine; only I cannot. What you cannot see: the display reads 0. The light is yellow. The keypad has four keys, left to right numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, it wants exactly one digit, none entered yet; the printed squiggles on the keys mean nothing to me either, so use positions only. Wires left to right: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green — go by position and thickness as you feel them. Our third, Mute, holds the manual but cannot speak and cannot touch; Mute can only reach me by gesture, and I relay instructions to you by voice. You CAN speak directly to Mute, but Mute cannot answer you — answers will come from me. Until I relay Mute's instruction, touch nothing, just hold position. If you feel anything change, sign me thumbs-down and then tell the room aloud what happened for Mute's sake.

What just happened is a huge unlock. Deaf heard nothing of my speech, but read my seven signs as an overture and answered by voice with a full visual share of the bomb: display 0, yellow light, four positional keys wanting one digit, wires red/yellow/green at 1/2/3 — plus a compact gesture vocabulary for me to use toward Deaf (thumbs-up done, thumbs-down stop, open palm waiting, fist touching). Deaf also corrected my routing model: my voice only ever reaches Mute, so anything for Mute I simply say aloud, and all manual knowledge must come back to me through Deaf's voice.

My situation now: I have the bomb's shape but not a single rule from the manual yet, so the correct hands-off behavior continues — I touch nothing. This turn I do two things. To Deaf, one clean sign: the open palm, meaning I hold and wait; using the code correctly is itself the confirmation that I adopted it, and Deaf watches my hands anyway, so status signs are all Deaf needs from me. To Mute, who went before me this round and so receives my words at the start of Mute's next turn, I send a consolidated state report — Mute may only see the manual and not the bomb, so Deaf's visual facts are worth relaying — together with four precisely numbered manual questions and the routing instruction: answers go by gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks them aloud, and only then do my hands move. I also state my sign code so Mute, who can see gestures, can follow my status signs too.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, holding still, nothing touched. Deaf has given me the visual report and we agreed a small sign code. Full state so far: the display reads 0; the indicator light is yellow; the keypad has four keys in a row at positions 1 to 4, it wants exactly one digit and nothing is entered yet, and the printed squiggles on the keys are uninterpreted even by Deaf; the wires at positions 1, 2, 3 are red, yellow and green, and I can also tell them apart by thickness. Please look up and answer four things. First, what the display reading 0 requires, if anything. Second, what a yellow light means or requires. Third, the rule that determines the one-digit keypad entry, and whether the key symbols matter to it. Fourth, the rule for cutting the red, yellow and green wires, including the order and whether the light or the display changes it. If the manual describes the keypad keys by their printed symbols, gesture a description of the symbols in the manual's order to Deaf, and Deaf can match them to the squiggles and tell me which position to press. Send all answers by gesture to Deaf, who will speak them aloud; I act only on Deaf's relayed instruction. My sign code with Deaf, which you can also see me make: thumbs-up means done, thumbs-down means problem and stop, raised open palm means waiting, fist means touching or pressing. I have just signed the open palm to Deaf to say I am holding.")
```

The press itself and its feel reach me fully only when my view updates next round — calls return nothing — so my spoken report to Mute now states exactly what is true at this moment: the press was made as instructed, and the full sound-and-feel report plus any display change (Deaf will see it) follows at the start of next round.
